unlock_procedure: 1. The operator puts a credential they own where their own git configuration can read it. This checkout has `credential.helper = manager` (Git Credential Manager), which only authenticates interactively, so any of these works and none of them requires a token in this chat or in this repository:
a. run `git push origin HEAD` once from an interactive terminal and complete the sign-in; the manager stores the credential in the operating system's vault and later non-interactive pushes reuse it;

b. pre-seed that vault without git prompting for a URL: pipe `protocol=https`, `host=github.com`, `username=<github user>` and `password=<fine-grained PAT with contents:write>` into `git credential-manager store` (the value never leaves the operator's machine and is never read or printed here);

c. set an exported token in the environment of the pushing process and let git read it from the environment only, e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN=... git -c credential.helper='!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo password=$GITHUB_TOKEN; }; f' push origin HEAD`;
d. install the GitHub CLI and let it configure git: `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https` followed by `gh auth setup-git`.
2. Verify the unlock without writing to the remote: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git push --dry-run origin HEAD` must exit 0 and print the ref update it would publish.
3. Publish the branch (it does not exist on the remote yet): `git push --set-upstream origin agent/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-00-baseline`.

4. Confirm from the remote, not from the local exit code: `git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/agent/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-00-baseline` must return the pushed commit, and its sha must equal `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Rules: never paste the credential into the chat, never commit it, and revoke it if it ever reaches a log. Nothing in this work package depends on the push: the campaign runs offline against local corpora and both verifiers read only published files.
push.secrets_handling: No token, password or credential value was read, printed, stored or requested. This record lists only the presence or absence of the mechanisms and the exact commands an operator can run.
